sceneText:
Sie brachten Roger zum See. Franziska lief mit Manuel bis ans Ufer – weiter liessen die Soldaten sie nicht.

Der Vierwaldstättersee war grau und schwer, die Wellen schlugen gegen die Steine. Die Soldaten stiessen Roger in ein kleines Boot und ruderten los.

Manuel stand am Ufer. Er wollte ins Wasser. Man sah es an seinen Schultern, an seinen geballten Fäusten. Aber Franziska stand neben ihm, schüttelte einmal den Kopf – ruhig, bestimmt. Und Manuel blieb.

Dann brach der Sturm los. Erst ein Brausen in den Wipfeln. Dann Wellen, gross wie Haustüren, und Regen, der waagrecht fiel.

Ultra-wide shot looking out across a vast grey lake from the shore. The surface of Lake Lucerne churns in the foreground — dark grey-green waves rolling in, white foam at the crests, rain slanting across the frame in diagonal lines. The far mountains across the lake are swallowed in cloud and mist. At the stone shore in the lower-left foreground, two tiny figures stand at the water's edge: Manuel — tall for fourteen, in his grey-green tunic, body turned slightly toward the water, both arms rigid at his sides. Beside him Franziska in her terracotta-orange dress and grey wool shawl, solid and still, her face turned toward Manuel. Both figures are very small — roughly a sixth of the frame height — the vastness of the lake and storm dominating the composition. A small wooden boat is visible in the left midground on the churning water, barely visible through rain. The sky is nearly black at the upper frame. Bottom-right corner deep dark churning water for text.

**COMPOSITION:**
- Characters must INTERACT with the scene — facing and engaging with objects, landmarks, or each other. NOT standing in front of a backdrop looking at the viewer.
- Characters face TOWARD what they interact with. Eyes look at objects or other characters, NOT at the camera.
- If a landmark, building, or object is in the BACKGROUND, characters must face AWAY from the camera toward it — we see their backs or sides as they look at it.

The bottom portion of the image, closest to the viewer, must show ONLY the natural ground of this scene — light cobblestones for a street, open floor for a room, calm water / grass / sand / snow / sky for outdoor scenes. No character bodies, feet, or shadows cutting into that strip if all characters are midground.

**COMPOSITION — DARK QUIET ZONE:** The lower left corner of the image (roughly 30%) must stay visually simple AND dark — intentional low-luminance negative space where white text will be placed. Continue the scene naturally into this area — same sky, same wall, same ground — but paint it in deep, shadowed tones of the scene's own palette (dusk sky, shadowed wall, deep water, dark foliage, unlit corner). No characters, no sharp lines, no high-contrast detail, no bright highlights in this zone.

**ART STYLE:** A traditional watercolor painting in the style of Inga Moore. Realistic human proportions across all ages — children look like children, teenagers look visibly older than children, adults look like adults. Textured paper with pencil underpainting, delicate color washes with wet-on-wet technique, soft paint edges, visible artistic brushstrokes, and transparent flowing colors. Warm but not overly vibrant color palette with visible paper texture throughout.
